claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
The multilevel chemical and microstructural fluctuations govern local stress distributions.
The multilevel chemical and microstructural fluctuations govern crack-initiation paths.
Coupling local RVE calculations to a machine-learning surrogate can approximate the global elastic response of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Coupling local RVE calculations to a machine-learning surrogate can approximate the global yield behavior of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Coupling local RVE calculations to a machine-learning surrogate can approximate the fracture toughness of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Targeted local experimental calibration can account for heterogeneity and compensate for reduced-order modeling approximations.
The hybrid framework can achieve accuracy comparable to full first-principles and CALPHAD approaches.
The framework is expected to predict Young's modulus within 5% error.
The framework is expected to predict yield strength within 10% error.
The framework is expected to predict toughness with approximately 10–20% uncertainty.
The framework is expected to reduce computational time by approximately 10-fold relative to detailed first-principles and CALPHAD approaches.
Existing full-scale first-principles, CALPHAD, and traditional machine-learning techniques require extensive computation.
Existing modeling techniques struggle to predict toughness accurately.
The framework may become unreliable at high strain rates.
The framework may become unreliable at elevated temperatures.
The framework may become unreliable after processing treatments that alter the hierarchical microstructure.
The framework may become unreliable when local RVEs are not representative of global behavior or when relevant phenomena fall outside the training data.

contradictions.description: Young's modulus is predicted to be within 5% error, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis above 10% error. Thus, an error between 5% and 10% would fail the stated quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
